sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Fulton County
sections.html:
Three offices are involved. The Treasurer, who is also the ex-officio County Collector, sends the bills and takes payment. The Supervisor of Assessments oversees values and exemptions. The Board of Review hears assessment complaints, and the Supervisor of Assessments serves as its clerk. Both main offices are in the Fulton County Courthouse, 100 N. Main Street, Lewistown. Canton, Cuba, Farmington, Lewistown and Astoria are all billed by the same Treasurer.

  • Treasurer/Collector: PO Box 111, Lewistown, IL 61542; (309) 547-3041, extension 132; counter open 8:00 am to 4:00 pm weekdays
  • Supervisor of Assessments: PO Box 283, same courthouse; same main number, extension 113; no lunch closure
  • Township assessors set values in townships that have one. In the rest, county deputy assessors do the yearly fieldwork.

sections.h2: Fulton County housing at a glance
sections.html: Fulton County is in west central Illinois, with Lewistown as the seat and Canton as the largest city. It's a lower-priced market with a shrinking population: 32,901 residents, 2.3% fewer than the 2020 base, in 15,869 housing units. Owners live in 76.6% of the homes. The typical owner-occupied home is worth $107,200, median gross rent is $785 and median household income is $60,599. At those values, an unpaid tax bill or a long repair list takes a bigger bite out of a sale price than it would in a costlier market.

sections.h2: How a Fulton County tax bill is figured
sections.html:
The formula on the Treasurer's bill insert is simple: equalized assessed value (EAV), minus exemptions, times the total local tax rate equals the bill. EAV is typically 33 1/3% of fair market value, adjusted by a state-mandated multiplier. School districts, the county, municipalities, townships and special districts such as park, library, fire protection and sanitary districts all take a share. Distributions to those taxing bodies go out every 30 days from the first due date.

Fulton County bills a year behind. Taxes on the 2024 assessment were mailed in 2025, with the first installment due June 13 and the second September 5. Each bill carries two payment stubs. Read the dates on your current bill, because a bill that never arrived is still owed.

The Treasurer takes payment in person, by mail, at most county banks, in a courthouse drop box, online and by phone. The counter accepts cash, personal checks, cashier's checks, money orders and cards, and cards carry a convenience fee. Each channel stops working at a different point in the year, which matters if a closing date slips.

Fulton County payment channels and cutoffs
ChannelHours or cutoff
Courthouse counterMonday to Friday, 8:00 am to 4:00 pm; bring the stubs
MailMust be postmarked on time; a postage meter imprint is not accepted as proof
Local banksBanking hours with stubs; unavailable once an installment is delinquent
Drop boxBack door of the courthouse; after 2:00 pm the payment takes the next day's date; no cash
OnlineStops after the second installment due date
CardsStop after the second installment due date
Personal checksStop once delinquent certified letters go out in September

Mail is now postmarked when the post office processes it, not when you drop it off, so a hand-stamp at a post office counter or an early mailing is the safer route. Returned checks carry a $25 fee.

Unpaid tax carries 1.5% interest for each month or part of a month, under 35 ILCS 200/21-15. The payment scale on each stub shows the penalty for each date range. Under 35 ILCS 200/21-135 the collector also adds $10 for certified mailing, advertising and publication costs.

  • 35 ILCS 200/20-25 lets the collector refuse a personal or corporate check within 45 days before a tax sale.
  • Unpaid parcels are published and certified letters go out. Then the Treasurer takes judgment from the circuit court and runs the delinquent tax sale.
  • The County Clerk figures rates and collects redemptions on sold taxes.

Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure by parcel number before any closing. The county's online property tax inquiry searches by parcel number, owner name, address, sale price or tax code, and prints the bill and payment history for each parcel.

Start by asking the township assessor or the county deputy assessors for an informal review, then file a complaint with the Board of Review if needed. The 30-day complaint window opens when your township's notice runs in the newspaper, and that date moves every year. A tax bill itself can't be appealed. After it arrives, only errors of fact, such as a missing exemption or wrong square footage, can be fixed through the Assessment Office.

The Board of Review rules matter if you're in the middle of a sale. The person filing must hold a legal interest at the time: a recorded deed, a recorded contract for deed or installment memorandum, or a purchase agreement fully signed by both parties. Complaints go in by hand, or by mail, courier or parcel service postmarked on or before the last filing day. Email and fax are refused.

  • Equity appeals compare similar nearby homes. Market value appeals rest on recent sales of comparable homes.
  • Useful evidence includes a realtor's market analysis, a certified appraisal, a comparable sheet, a closing statement and photographs.
  • After a tentative decision and a hearing, a final notice goes out. From that notice's postmark, you have 30 days to go to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board.

Fulton County lists seven homestead exemptions, and the owner has to apply for each one. Check your bill every year to confirm you're getting all you qualify for.

  • General Homestead Exemption for owner-occupied residences
  • Senior Citizen Homestead Exemption for owners over 65
  • Senior Citizens Assessment Freeze Exemption, which holds assessed value at a base year, with income limits. It does not freeze the tax bill amount.
  • Homestead Improvement Exemption for value added by a new improvement on a parcel that also has the general exemption
  • Returning Veteran's, Disabled Veteran's (at least 50% service-connected disability certified by the VA) and Disabled Persons' exemptions

A new owner-occupant should ask the Assessment Office, extension 113, which filings are needed once the deed is recorded. A seller who moved out midyear can ask the same office how that year's exemption is handled.

sections.h2: Selling with unpaid or unclear tax
sections.html:
Begin with the parcel number, printed at the top left of the bill and searchable online. Work through these steps:

  • Pull the payment history and confirm which installments are open.
  • Ask the Treasurer for the total owed with penalties through the expected closing date, and get it in writing.
  • Take the Assessment Office any exemption that should be on the parcel, since an error of fact can be corrected after the bill is issued.
  • Give the title company the payoff so the tax is paid from proceeds at closing.

A house with deferred repairs, back taxes or an estate attached can sit on the market where values are this modest. Some owners choose a direct as-is sale to a cash buyer, which skips repairs and puts the tax settlement into the contract. On any route, the written payoff is what keeps the closing on schedule.

faqs.q: When are Fulton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: In two installments, with dates that change yearly. The 2024 taxes payable in 2025 were due June 13 and September 5. The stubs on your current bill carry the live dates, or call (309) 547-3041, extension 132.

faqs.q: Who sends the Fulton County tax bill?
faqs.a: The County Treasurer, who is also ex-officio County Collector, prints and mails it. The County Clerk works out the rates and the Assessor sets values and approves exemptions. If nothing arrives, call the Treasurer anyway.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Fulton County taxes late?
faqs.a: Interest of 1.5% accrues for each month or part of a month, under 35 ILCS 200/21-15. A $10 mailing and publication charge applies under 35 ILCS 200/21-135, and each stub prints a scale of amounts by date range.

faqs.q: How long do Fulton County owners have to appeal an assessment?
faqs.a: Thirty days from the newspaper publication for your township, and that date shifts yearly. File with the Supervisor of Assessments by hand or postmarked mail. The Property Tax Appeal Board has its own 30-day clock from the final notice's postmark.

faqs.q: Can someone under contract to buy a Fulton County house file an assessment complaint?
faqs.a: Yes, if the purchase agreement is fully signed by both parties. The Board of Review also accepts a recorded deed, a recorded installment memorandum or a contract for deed as a qualifying legal interest.
